Definition: Estimated financial cost to business of not keeping data for compliance/regulation purposes.
A count of records with a fixed value per record can be used.
For intellectual property data assets whose value is directly proportional to its financial value (e.g. licences or patents).
Estimated financial cost to business of maintaining, adapting or curating data.
Price that a user will accept for data, sometimes in return for a specific service.
Estimated financial cost to create, replace or reproduce this data.
Estimated financial cost to business of not having access to data or a service based on observations in the data.
Estimated financial cost to business of competitors having access to data.
Estimated financial cost to business of storing data.
For visual sensors, a measure of the potential accuracy of sensor readings from a specific source.
Data records that describe or refer to specific customers, for example business transactions with that customer, may be weighted. Typically used with count of records.
The financial amount of a transaction recorded in a field of a data record may be used as a weight for the value of that record. Typically used with count of records.
An estimate of the quality of an image based on camera type, brightness, contrast, resolution, noise, and exposition.
A measure of the uniqueness of data in the dataset.

By classifying the contents of an image or sensor reading to a set of events with known probabilities, this calculates the information measure of the image containing a specific event. Alternatively, a Fisher Information Matrix (FIM)-based metric may be used.
For K-nearest neighbours classifier algorithms, the Shapley value of the KNN utility of each data point can be calculated.
A measure of the fraction of most unique words in a file compared to the contents of the whole collection.
A qualification of the inferential gain by increasing the size or features of data when comparing two datasets.
The probability that other organisations, particularly competitors and partners, have the same data.
A time series measure weighted towards data most recently created.
An access time series measure based on how often data is read and written to.
A measure of the degree of usage.
An estimate of the number of similar users in the system compared to the ones that have accessed the data, and that are hence likely to also access the data.
A measure of the significance of the type of usage.
Data valuation based on read and write granularity, data distribution, and data association.
A specialised time-based metric to capture when data was last used.
The number of unique users that access the data.
A measure of the significance of the usage based on user role.
A quantification of value based on the usage of the data over time.
Usefulness of sample data for a given inferential task.
For end-of-life processing (recycle, parts reuse, product reuse), an estimate of goods condition is needed.
Price that a user will accept for data, sometimes in return for a specific service.
Number of approvals ('kudos') given to a message by the community.
A measure that calculates the relative utility of a dataset by comparing the differences between original data of a personal nature and an obfuscated version of the same data.
An assessment of the value of a data item by the provider of that data.
The number of business processes that use, or could benefit from this data.
Revenue increases or decreases with or without access to the data.
Estimated financial cost to business of competitors having access to data.
Reduced or improved service outcomes with or without access to the data.
For vehicular sensors, a measure of the distance where sensor readings become increasingly important.
An assessment of the value of a data item by the user of that data after consuming it.
Priority given to a data item by a specific user.
